final_text:
**Claim 1746933 (DME claim) has a denial-risk score of 0.2705.** The validation-set average is 0.1805. That puts the claim 1.5 times the average, or 9.0 percentage points above it. The model's baseline probability is 0.1404.

**What the model weighs most:**
- **HCPCS_CD = A7038** (procedure/service code billed) raises the score the most. It has a SHAP value of 0.588 log-odds, which is an 80% increase in the odds. The tools don't say what this code means, so I won't say.
- **PRVDR_NUM = 314019** (billing provider identifier) also raises it, by 0.304 log-odds, a 36% increase in the odds.
- **LINE_PLACE_OF_SRVC_CD = 11**, **CARR_CLM_BLG_NPI_NUM**, and **TAX_NUM** each lower the score slightly. **ORG_NPI_NUM** raises it slightly. None of these four has an entry in the project data dictionary, so I can't describe their meaning. They are native CMS claim fields.

The 153 features not shown are not itemized. Together with the six above they make up the rest of the score.

These values show what the model weighs. They don't show what causes a denial. The denial label in this project is synthetic, built from risk rules, so the score is not a real payer decision.

I didn't run a policy search, because you asked only about the score. I can look up whether the policy documents cover this code if you'd like.
